name: Go
typeSystem: Static, strong, mostly inferred. Deliberately small: structural interfaces instead of inheritance, and (since Go 1.18) parametric generics with type constraints.

typeSystemExample.caption: Generic max with a type constraint (Go 1.18+)

runtime: Compiled ahead-of-time to native code and linked with the Go runtime (goroutine scheduler and garbage collector). Binaries are often self-contained, but builds using facilities such as cgo may have dynamic-library dependencies.

runtimes.name: Native (gc toolchain)
runtimes.role: Official toolchain; produces native binaries linked with the Go scheduler and garbage collector.

runtimes.name: Native (gccgo)
runtimes.role: GCC-based frontend that reuses GCC's optimiser and back-end targets.

runtimes.name: WebAssembly (js/wasm, wasip1)
runtimes.role: Compiles Go to WASM for browsers and WASI runtimes.

runtimes.name: yaegi
runtimes.role: Interpreter used for scripting and plugins where a build step is undesirable.

compilers.name: gc
compilers.role: The compiler used by the official Go toolchain; the toolchain also supplies the linker and runtime.

compilers.name: gccgo
compilers.role: Alternative frontend built on GCC, sharing its optimisation passes.

compilers.name: TinyGo
compilers.role: LLVM-based compiler for microcontrollers and small WASM binaries.

concurrencyModel: Concurrency is a core feature: goroutines are lightweight tasks multiplexed by the runtime onto OS threads, and channels support CSP-inspired communication between them.

concurrencyExample.caption: 4 concurrent goroutines computing i*i and sending results on a channel
